government.note: De facto state in the north of Georgia; Georgia regards it as part of its territory. Its institutions are recorded factually: under the constitution of 27 November 1996 (per the article on the 1999 parliamentary election) a directly elected President with a five-year term, renewable once, who holds most political power, and a Prime Minister (Chairman of the Government) nominated by the President and appointed by Parliament (per the Wikipedia articles on the President and Prime Minister of South Ossetia and the 2026 presidential election).

system.note: seats_2000 is the result of the May 1999 election (33 seats, four reserved for the Georgian minority and left vacant). From 2004 the Parliament has 34 seats; 15 party-list, 15 single-member and 4 reserved seats in 2004, and 17 party-list plus 17 single-member seats today (per the 2004 election and Parliament articles). The seat count here is the 2000 size because seats_2000 must match it. The 2009 election was fully party-list with a 7% threshold.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the May 1999 parliamentary election, for which the source gives only approximate shares: Communist Party of South Ossetia about 80%, independents about 20% (recorded as big tent). President Lyudvig Chibirov was an independent and the Communist-led Parliament was in opposition to him, so no ruling party is listed.
